questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which artifact best shows that a student can organize a spoken message?

answer.text: A. A speaking outline with purpose, audience, main points, and transitions.

feedback.text: Correct. This artifact shows planning for clear oral communication and helps the reviewer see speaking organization.

answer.text: B. A photo with no caption.

feedback.text: This does not show speaking organization. A portfolio artifact needs evidence of the communication skill.

answer.text: C. A blank file labeled speech.

feedback.text: A label alone does not show skill. The artifact must contain meaningful planning or performance evidence.

answer.text: D. A list of unrelated topics.

feedback.text: Topics alone do not show organized speaking. The reviewer needs purpose, structure, and audience connection.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.01

Which portfolio reflection best explains a slide deck?

answer.text: A. I used blue on the slides because I like blue.

feedback.text: This focuses on preference, not presentation skill. Reflection should explain communication choices.

answer.text: B. The slide deck has many slides, so it is strong.

feedback.text: Quantity does not guarantee quality. Strong slides support the speaker and audience.

answer.text: C. The slide deck is in the folder, so it is finished.

feedback.text: Completion alone does not prove mastery. The reflection must explain what the artifact demonstrates.

answer.text: D. The slide deck shows how I used visuals and headings to support a spoken presentation for a specific audience.

feedback.text: Correct. This reflection connects the artifact to presentation planning and audience understanding.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.01

Which artifact best shows research-supported communication?

answer.text: A. A list of opinions with no sources.

feedback.text: This does not show research skill because no source evidence is included or explained.

answer.text: B. Briefing notes with a research question, source evidence, and source explanation.

feedback.text: Correct. This artifact shows how research was selected and used to support a communication purpose.

answer.text: C. A title page with the word research on it.

feedback.text: A title is not evidence of research-supported communication.

answer.text: D. A decorative border around the portfolio.

feedback.text: Design may help presentation, but it does not show research-supported communication by itself.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.DIG.01

Which explanation best shows digital publication skill?

answer.text: A. The file is online, so it is automatically effective.

feedback.text: Being online is not enough. Digital communication requires audience-aware format, design, and clarity.

answer.text: B. The publication has many colors, so the audience will understand it.

feedback.text: Colors alone do not ensure understanding. Design must support the message.

answer.text: C. The digital flyer uses headings, readable contrast, and a clear next step for the audience.

feedback.text: Correct. This explanation connects design and organization to audience use.

answer.text: D. The publication is long, so it contains everything.

feedback.text: Length can overload the audience. Digital publication should be clear and usable.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.01

What should the portfolio introduction do?

answer.text: A. Focus only on how difficult the work was.

feedback.text: Effort may be part of reflection, but the introduction should explain communication evidence.

answer.text: B. Hide the purpose until the end.

feedback.text: This makes the portfolio harder to understand. Communication should guide the audience clearly.

answer.text: C. List every file without explanation.

feedback.text: A list does not show why artifacts matter. The introduction should explain purpose and organization.

answer.text: D. Explain the portfolio purpose, audience, and skills the reviewer should notice.

feedback.text: Correct. The introduction orients the reviewer and makes the portfolio easier to evaluate.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.02

Which portfolio organization best supports the reviewer?

answer.text: A. Put artifacts in a random order.

feedback.text: Random order makes the portfolio harder to follow. Organization should help the reviewer see skill development.

answer.text: B. Group artifacts by skill, such as speaking, research, presentation, and digital communication.

feedback.text: Correct. This organization helps the reviewer understand what each artifact demonstrates.

answer.text: C. Hide the strongest artifact in the middle with no label.

feedback.text: This makes evidence harder to find. Clear labels and organization support the audience.

answer.text: D. Remove all headings to make the portfolio shorter.

feedback.text: Headings help the reviewer navigate. Removing them can reduce clarity.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.03

Which reflection is most audience-aware?

answer.text: A. I chose this artifact because I wanted to include it.

feedback.text: This explains preference, not audience value. Audience-aware reflection tells the reviewer what the artifact proves.

answer.text: B. I included this because it was easy to find.

feedback.text: This is not a communication reason. The artifact should be selected for what it demonstrates.

answer.text: C. I included this because it helps the reviewer see how I adapted tone and details for families and students.

feedback.text: Correct. This reflection names audience adaptation and explains why the artifact matters.

answer.text: D. I included this because it is the first file in my folder.

feedback.text: File order is not evidence of communication skill. Selection should be purposeful.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which artifact would be weakest for proving speaking readiness?

answer.text: A. A recorded speech reflection with notes about pacing and clarity.

feedback.text: This can show speaking readiness because it reflects on delivery and improvement.

answer.text: B. A speech outline with transitions and audience notes.

feedback.text: This can show speaking organization and audience planning.

answer.text: C. Speaker notes that explain when to cite evidence aloud.

feedback.text: This can show speaking preparation and responsible source use.

answer.text: D. A file name that says final speech but contains no content.

feedback.text: Correct. A file name alone does not provide evidence of speaking readiness.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.01

Why should a presentation artifact include speaker notes or explanation?

answer.text: A. They show how the speaker planned to explain visuals and guide the audience.

feedback.text: Correct. Speaker notes reveal communication thinking that a slide alone may not show.

answer.text: B. They make the slide deck longer without adding meaning.

feedback.text: Length is not the goal. Notes should clarify the connection between visuals and speech.

answer.text: C. They replace the need for audience awareness.

feedback.text: Notes should include audience awareness, not replace it.

answer.text: D. They prove every slide is perfect.

feedback.text: Notes do not prove perfection. They show planning and reasoning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.01

Which reflection best explains a research artifact?

answer.text: A. This source is included because it was the first result.

feedback.text: This does not explain relevance or quality. The reflection should connect the source to the message.

answer.text: B. These notes show how I used source evidence to support a professional recommendation.

feedback.text: Correct. This reflection explains how the artifact demonstrates research-supported communication.

answer.text: C. I copied a source, so research is complete.

feedback.text: Copying does not show source explanation. Research must be used responsibly and connected to the claim.

answer.text: D. I included research because every portfolio needs research.

feedback.text: This is generic and does not explain what the artifact proves.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.DIG.01

Which digital artifact would best show audience-aware design?

answer.text: A. A flyer with tiny text and no headings.

feedback.text: This is not audience-aware because it is difficult to read and scan.

answer.text: B. A page with all key details hidden in images.

feedback.text: This makes information harder to access. Key details should be readable.

answer.text: C. An announcement with clear headings, readable contrast, and an obvious next step.

feedback.text: Correct. This artifact shows digital design choices that support audience understanding.

answer.text: D. A decorative background with no message.

feedback.text: Decoration alone does not communicate. A digital artifact must serve a purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.01

Which sentence best states a portfolio purpose?

answer.text: A. This portfolio has some things from class.

feedback.text: This is vague. A purpose statement should explain what the portfolio is meant to show.

answer.text: B. This portfolio is here because it was assigned.

feedback.text: This explains compliance, not communication purpose.

answer.text: C. This portfolio is probably finished now.

feedback.text: This does not orient the reviewer or explain the skills shown.

answer.text: D. This portfolio shows my readiness to plan, present, research, and adapt communication for different audiences.

feedback.text: Correct. This purpose statement clearly tells the reviewer what the portfolio demonstrates.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.02

Which choice best supports coherent portfolio flow?

answer.text: A. Introduce the portfolio, group artifacts by skill, and explain each artifact before moving to the next.

feedback.text: Correct. This structure guides the reviewer through purpose, evidence, and reflection.

answer.text: B. Begin with unlabeled artifacts and end with the introduction.

feedback.text: This makes the reviewer work too hard. The introduction should orient the audience first.

answer.text: C. Use no headings because the reviewer can figure it out.

feedback.text: This weakens clarity. Headings support navigation and organization.

answer.text: D. Place reflections in a separate folder without labels.

feedback.text: This separates evidence from explanation and makes the portfolio harder to evaluate.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.03

Which portfolio choice best reflects audience awareness?

answer.text: A. Use unexplained abbreviations the reviewer may not know.

feedback.text: This can confuse the audience. Audience-aware portfolios use clear language.

answer.text: B. Assume the reviewer knows what every artifact means.

feedback.text: The reviewer needs explanation. Reflection should make the evidence clear.

answer.text: C. Add labels and reflections that explain the communication skill shown by each artifact.

feedback.text: Correct. Labels and reflections help the reviewer understand the purpose and value of the work.

answer.text: D. Remove context to make the portfolio shorter.

feedback.text: Shorter is not always clearer. The audience needs enough context to understand the artifacts.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which reflection best shows growth in speaking?

answer.text: A. I got this speech done quickly.

feedback.text: Speed does not show communication growth. Reflection should connect to speaking skill.

answer.text: B. This outline shows how I improved my organization by adding transitions and audience-focused examples.

feedback.text: Correct. This explains a specific speaking skill and shows growth in planning.

answer.text: C. This speech was hard, so it should be included.

feedback.text: Difficulty alone does not prove mastery. The reflection should explain what skill improved.

answer.text: D. This artifact is long, so it shows growth.

feedback.text: Length does not guarantee speaking growth. The reflection should name the communication improvement.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.01

Which slide artifact best belongs in the portfolio?

answer.text: A. A slide deck with unrelated images and no explanation.

feedback.text: This does not show purposeful presentation planning. Visuals should support the message.

answer.text: B. A slide deck with every word of the speech copied onto slides.

feedback.text: This can overload the audience. Presentation artifacts should show visual support, not script copying.

answer.text: C. A slide deck with no title, no order, and no audience connection.

feedback.text: This lacks organization and audience awareness.

answer.text: D. A slide deck with clear headings, relevant visuals, and notes explaining audience choices.

feedback.text: Correct. This artifact shows presentation planning, audience awareness, and visual support.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.01

What should a research artifact prove?

answer.text: A. The student can select evidence and explain how it supports a communication purpose.

feedback.text: Correct. Research in speech communication must be connected to claims, audience, and purpose.

answer.text: B. The student can paste source titles without reading them.

feedback.text: This does not show research skill. The artifact must explain how sources support the message.

answer.text: C. The student can avoid explaining evidence.

feedback.text: Evidence needs explanation so the audience understands the reasoning.

answer.text: D. The student can use any source regardless of relevance.

feedback.text: Source relevance matters. Research should support the communication purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.DIG.01

Why should a digital artifact include a clear next step?

answer.text: A. It makes the artifact more confusing.

feedback.text: A clear next step should reduce confusion, not increase it.

answer.text: B. It helps the audience know what to do after reading or viewing the message.

feedback.text: Correct. Digital communication often needs action, so the next step supports usability.

answer.text: C. It replaces the need for readable design.

feedback.text: The next step is important, but the design still needs to be readable and accessible.

answer.text: D. It proves the artifact is longer.

feedback.text: Length is not the goal. The next step should be clear and useful.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.01

Which portfolio statement is clearest?

answer.text: A. Here are files from class.

feedback.text: This is too general. It does not explain the portfolio's purpose or skills.

answer.text: B. This is everything I could find.

feedback.text: This suggests random selection rather than purposeful communication.

answer.text: C. This portfolio shows my ability to plan spoken, researched, and digital communication for specific audiences.

feedback.text: Correct. This statement clearly identifies the purpose and major skills.

answer.text: D. Look through this and decide what it means.

feedback.text: This puts too much work on the reviewer. Communication should guide the audience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.02

Which item should be paired with each portfolio artifact?

answer.text: A. A reflection explaining the communication skill it demonstrates.

feedback.text: Correct. Reflection helps the reviewer understand why the artifact matters.

answer.text: B. No explanation, so the artifact speaks for itself.

feedback.text: Artifacts may not be self-explanatory. The reviewer needs context and reflection.

answer.text: C. A note saying the artifact was required.

feedback.text: Requirement does not explain mastery. Reflection should name the skill.

answer.text: D. A decorative icon only.

feedback.text: An icon may help design, but it does not explain the communication value.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.03

Which choice best adapts a portfolio for a professional reviewer?

answer.text: A. Use clear labels, respectful tone, concise explanations, and organized sections.

feedback.text: Correct. These choices help a professional reviewer understand the portfolio efficiently.

answer.text: B. Use slang and unexplained class jokes.

feedback.text: This may confuse the reviewer and weaken professional tone.

answer.text: C. Hide explanations to make the reviewer guess.

feedback.text: This is not audience-aware. The portfolio should guide the reader.

answer.text: D. Include every draft without selecting the strongest evidence.

feedback.text: Purposeful selection is more useful than overwhelming the reviewer.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which speaking artifact best shows audience adaptation?

answer.text: A. Notes that use the same examples for every audience.

feedback.text: This does not show adaptation. Audience examples should fit listeners' needs.

answer.text: B. Speaking notes that explain why examples were chosen for a specific audience.

feedback.text: Correct. This shows the speaker considered listeners when preparing the message.

answer.text: C. A script with no audience information.

feedback.text: A script may show wording, but it does not prove audience adaptation without context.

answer.text: D. A timer screenshot with no explanation.

feedback.text: Timing can matter, but this artifact alone does not show audience adaptation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.01

What is the strongest reason to include a presentation plan?

answer.text: A. It proves the student can make slides colorful.

feedback.text: Color alone is not presentation mastery. The plan should show how visuals support communication.

answer.text: B. It shows the student has a file to submit.

feedback.text: Having a file does not prove skill. The artifact must show planning and reasoning.

answer.text: C. It shows how the student organized visual support, speaker notes, and audience-focused delivery.

feedback.text: Correct. This demonstrates planning for a complete presentation experience.

answer.text: D. It replaces the need for speaking skill.

feedback.text: Presentation planning supports speaking, but it does not replace the speaker's communication choices.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.01

Which research reflection is strongest?

answer.text: A. I found a source, so my research is complete.

feedback.text: This is incomplete. The reflection should explain how the source supports communication.

answer.text: B. The source looked official, so I used it without explanation.

feedback.text: This does not show reasoning. The speaker must explain relevance and support.

answer.text: C. Research was required, so I added it.

feedback.text: This focuses on assignment completion rather than communication skill.

answer.text: D. This source helped me support my recommendation because it gave evidence about audience needs.

feedback.text: Correct. This reflection connects source evidence to a recommendation and audience purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U06_L07_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.DIG.01

Which final portfolio check is best?

answer.text: A. Ask whether each artifact is labeled, explained, and connected to a communication skill.

feedback.text: Correct. This check ensures the portfolio is purposeful and understandable for the reviewer.

answer.text: B. Ask whether the portfolio has the most files possible.

feedback.text: More files do not guarantee mastery. Purposeful selection matters more than quantity.

answer.text: C. Ask whether the portfolio avoids all reflection.

feedback.text: Reflection is necessary so the reviewer understands what each artifact proves.

answer.text: D. Ask whether the portfolio uses no organization.

feedback.text: Organization helps the reviewer follow the portfolio and see growth.
